zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ṭalāq (Divorce)
Medinan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ إذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ﴾ — this is an address to the Prophet ﷺ, and the believers are included with him in the address. Its meaning is: "if you intend divorce," just as He said: ﴿إذا قُمْتُمْ إلى الصَّلاةِ﴾ [al-Māʾida: 6], meaning: when you intend to stand for the prayer.

His saying: ﴿فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ وأحْصُوا العِدَّةَ﴾ — the divorce of the Sunna (the one agreed upon, in the view of Mālik: that a man divorce his wife while she is in a state of purity, without intercourse, with a single pronouncement, then leave her, if he wishes to persist in separating from her, for three menstrual periods. When she enters the third menstruation he no longer has the right to take her back; but if he wishes and she wishes to renew a fresh marriage contract, that is open to them both. [Translator's note: the opening parenthesis is in the source and is not closed there.] This is because the meaning of ﴿لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أمْرًا﴾ is: after the single divorce. If he divorces her three times at one time, there is no sense in His saying ﴿لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أمْرًا﴾, for its interpretation is only the taking back — I mean, when the three occur at one time. This is the view of Mālik, may Allah have mercy on him. The people of Iraq said: if he divorces her while she is pure without intercourse, then pronounces one divorce at each menstruation, that too is in their view a divorce of the Sunna; and if he does what Mālik said, that too is Sunna in their view. Al-Shāfiʿī said: if he divorces her while she is pure without intercourse, he is also divorcing according to the Sunna, whether he pronounces one or three; but with this, when it is three, His saying ﴿لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ أمْرًا﴾ falls away. Severity has come regarding whoever oversteps the divorce of the Sunna, for He said: ﴿ذَلِكم يُوعَظُ بِهِ مَن كانَ يُؤْمِنُ بِاللَّهِ واليَوْمِ الآخِرِ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 2], and He said: ﴿وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ﴾, meaning by the limits of Allah the limits of the divorce of the Sunna and what is mentioned along with divorce.

His saying: ﴿وَلا يَخْرُجْنَ إلا أنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ﴾ — it is also read ”مُبَيَّنَةٍ“. So He granted lodging to divorced women. It is said that their going out of their houses is itself an indecency; and it is said that ”اَلْفاحِشَةُ المُبَيِّنَةُ“ is fornication, the proof of this view being His saying: ﴿واللاتِي يَأْتِينَ الفاحِشَةَ مِن نِسائِكُمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 15], meaning fornication. It is also said that ﴿إلا أنْ يَأْتِينَ بِفاحِشَةٍ مُبَيِّنَةٍ﴾ means fornication, theft or drinking wine; and it is said: everything for which a ḥadd (prescribed penalty) is due is an indecency.

zajjaj:2-3.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا﴾ ﴿وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِن حَيْثُ لا يَحْتَسِبُ﴾ — its meaning is: He will make for him a way out from the unlawful to the lawful; and it is also said: from the Fire to Paradise. ”وَيَرْزُقْهُ مِن حَيْثُ لا يَحْتَسِبُ“ — its meaning, and Allah knows best, is that if he fears Allah and prefers what is lawful and patience with his family when he is in straitened circumstances, Allah will open (the way) for him and provide for him from where he does not reckon. And it is possible that it means: if he fears Allah in his divorce, prefers what is with Allah and proceeds in it according to the Sunna, Allah will provide him with a wife in place of his wife.

His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ بالِغُ أمْرِهِ﴾ — it is also read ”بالِغٌ أمْرَهُ“, i.e. Allah attains what He wills. And it was read ”إنَّ اللَّهَ بالِغٌ أمْرُهُ“, with ”الأمر“ nominative through ”بالِغٌ“, i.e. Allah's command reaches (its goal) and is carried out.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿قَدْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدْرًا﴾, and ”قَدَرًا“ — i.e. an appointed time and a term.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
His saying: ﴿واللائِي يَئِسْنَ مِنَ المَحِيضِ مِن نِسائِكم إنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلاثَةُ أشْهُرٍ﴾ — it is said in some exegesis that they asked, saying: "We know the waiting period (ʿidda) of the woman who menstruates; what then is the waiting period of the one who does not menstruate, and of the one who has not menstruated?" So it was said: if you are in doubt — i.e. when you are in doubt — their waiting period is three months. What Mālik holds, and what the language indicates, is that its meaning is: "If you are in doubt about her menstruation, her menses having stopped while she is of those like whom women menstruate, her waiting period is three months." That is after she has been left nine months, the length of a pregnancy; then after that she observes a waiting period of three months. If she menstruates within these three months, she completes three menstrual periods; and it is possible that this menstruation is delayed, so that whenever she is about to come out of the three (months) she menstruates. This is the doctrine of Mālik, and it is what is transmitted from ʿUmar, may Allah have mercy on him. The people of Iraq said: she is left (waiting) even if that reaches more than thirty years, even if she reaches seventy — meaning until she reaches the age of those who do not menstruate; and they said: had Allah willed, He could have tried her with more than that. Likewise His saying ﴿واللائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ﴾: its meaning, according to Mālik, is: if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months. The woman in despair (of menses), according to Mālik and others by consensus, is the one who has despaired of menstruation, about whom there is no doubt that she does not menstruate; she observes a waiting period of three months. The Quran contains no explicit text on that, but the Quran contains an indication of it, and I will explain it, if Allah wills. As for the young girl with whom intercourse is not (normally) had: if he consummates with her and has intercourse with her on the spot, he has only injured her, and according to Mālik there is no waiting period for her unless she is of an age at which intercourse is proper; according to him she is only counted among those with whom marriage has not been consummated. What is in the Quran indicates that the woman in despair (of menses) about whom there is no doubt must observe a waiting period of three months, because of His saying: ﴿واللائِي يَئِسْنَ مِنَ المَحِيضِ مِن نِسائِكم إنِ ارْتَبْتُمْ فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلاثَةُ أشْهُرٍ واللائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ﴾. Its meaning is: "and those who do not menstruate, their waiting period is three months"; so the analogy of ”اَللّائِي لا يَحِضْنَ“ (those who do not menstruate) is the analogy of ”اَللّائِي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ“ (those who have not menstruated), and there was no need to mention it. And if the waiting period of the one about whom there is doubt is three months, then the one about whom there is no doubt is all the more fitting for it.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَأُولاتُ الأحْمالِ أجَلُهُنَّ أنْ يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ﴾ means: their term for the severance of what is between them and their husbands is that they deliver their burden.

zajjaj:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿أسْكِنُوهُنَّ مِن حَيْثُ سَكَنْتُمْ مِن وُجْدِكُمْ﴾ — it is also read ”مِن وِجْدِكُمْ“. One says ”وَجَدْتُ في المالِ وُجْدًا“, i.e. I became a man of wealth, and ”وِجْدًا“ and ”جِدَةً“; and ”وَجَدْتُ الضّالَّةَ، وِجْدانًا“ (I found the stray animal); and ”وَجَدْتُ عَلى فُلانٍ وجْدًا“ and ”وَجَدْتُ عَلَيْهِ مَوْجِدَةً“ (I was angry with so-and-so). So Allah the Exalted made lodging obligatory until the waiting period ends. Lodging and maintenance (are due from the husband when he divorces with the divorce of the Sunna, until three menstrual periods have passed. If he makes the divorce irrevocable before the waiting period ends, he owes maintenance and lodging in the view of the people of Iraq, and he owes lodging (only) in the doctrine of Mālik and al-Shāfiʿī. [Translator's note: the opening parenthesis is in the source and is not closed there; «أبَتِ الطلاقَ» is printed as written and is understood here as أبَتَّ الطلاقَ, "made the divorce irrevocable".] As for the pregnant woman, he owes her maintenance, and that is explicit in the Quran in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَإنْ كُنَّ أُولاتِ حَمْلٍ فَأنْفِقُوا عَلَيْهِنَّ حَتّى يَضَعْنَ حَمْلَهُنَّ﴾.

His saying: ﴿فَإنْ أرْضَعْنَ لَكم فَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ﴾ means: give them the wage for their suckling. ﴿وَأْتَمِرُوا بَيْنَكم بِمَعْرُوفٍ﴾ — it is said in the exegesis that it is clothing and covering. And "what is right" (”اَلْمَعْرُوفُ“) — Allah knows best — is that the man should not fall short in the maintenance of the wet-nurse who suckles his child, when she is its mother, because the mother is more tender towards her child than anyone else, so she will not fall short in suckling it and seeing to its affairs. So it is the duty of each of them to consult together about the child in what is right. ﴿وَإنْ تَعاسَرْتُمْ فَسَتُرْضِعُ لَهُ أُخْرى﴾ means: let the father have someone other than the child's mother suckle it. This is a statement with the meaning of a command, because the wording of ﴿فَسَتُرْضِعُ لَهُ أُخْرى﴾ is the wording of a statement while its meaning is "let (another) suckle." Like it in having the wording of a statement and the meaning of a command is His saying: ﴿والوالِداتُ يُرْضِعْنَ أوْلادَهُنَّ حَوْلَيْنِ كامِلَيْنِ﴾ [al-Baqara: 233], meaning: let them suckle their children two full years.

zajjaj:7-7.t:
His saying: ﴿لِيُنْفِقْ ذُو سَعَةٍ مِن سَعَتِهِ﴾ — He commanded people of means to be generous towards their wives who suckle their children, according to the extent of their means [Translator's note: the pronoun in «سعتهن» is feminine in the text]. ﴿وَمَن قُدِرَ عَلَيْهِ رِزْقُهُ فَلْيُنْفِقْ مِمّا آتاهُ اللَّهُ﴾ means: whoever's provision is the measure of bare sustenance, let him spend according to that, as He said: ﴿عَلى المُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ وعَلى المُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ﴾ [al-Baqara: 236]. ﴿لا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إلا ما آتاها﴾ means: except what He has given it.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿سَيَجْعَلُ اللَّهُ بَعْدَ عُسْرٍ يُسْرًا﴾ — Allah made known to the believers that even though they were in straitened circumstances — and it is said that poverty and want prevailed over most of them at that time, in the days of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ — He, Mighty and Majestic, made known to them that the Muslims would become well off. And Allah opened (the world) to them after that and made ease after hardship.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَكَأيِّنْ مِن قَرْيَةٍ عَتَتْ عَنْ أمْرِ رَبِّها ورُسُلِهِ فَحاسَبْناها حِسابًا شَدِيدًا وعَذَّبْناها عَذابًا نُكْرًا﴾ means: We hastened the punishment for it. Its meaning is: its people were insolent, so We called its people to account and punished them.

zajjaj:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿فَذاقَتْ وبالَ أمْرِها وكانَ عاقِبَةُ أمْرِها خُسْرًا﴾ — i.e. the weight of the consequence of its conduct. ﴿وَكانَ عاقِبَةُ أمْرِها خُسْرًا﴾ means in the Hereafter, and that is His saying: ﴿أعَدَّ اللَّهُ لَهم عَذابًا شَدِيدًا﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 10], meaning after what befell them in this world. Then Allah admonished this community regarding believing the Prophet ﷺ and following his command, and made known that He had sent His Messenger to bring people out of darkness into light, and said: ﴿فاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ يا أُولِي الألْبابِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 10]. The meaning of ”أُولِي الألْبابِ“ is: people of intellect; the singular of ”أُولُو الألْبابِ“ is ”ذُو لُبٍّ“, i.e. one possessed of intellect. ﴿قَدْ أنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ إلَيْكم ذِكْرًا﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 10] ﴿رَسُولا يَتْلُو عَلَيْكم آياتِ اللَّهِ مُبَيِّناتٍ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 11] — ”رَسُولًا“ is accusative in three ways. The best of them is that His saying ﴿قَدْ أنْـزَلَ اللَّهُ إلَيْكم ذِكْرًا﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 10] indicates an implied "He sent a messenger who recites to you." It is also possible that by ”رَسُولًا“ He means the Prophet ﷺ, and that ”رَسُولًا“ is accusative through His saying ”ذِكْرًا“, the meaning being: "Allah has sent down to you a reminder, a messenger who brings a reminder, a messenger who recites." And ”رَسُولًا“ may be a badal (substitute) for ”ذِكْرًا“, Jibrīl (peace be upon him) being meant by it; the proof of this view is His saying — meaning by it Jibrīl, peace be upon him —: ﴿نَـزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الأمِينُ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 193] ﴿عَلى قَلْبِكَ﴾ [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 194]. [Translator's note: the text says "three ways" but then states the second as two sub-options (accusative through ذكرًا, or badal from ذكرًا).] The meaning of ﴿مِنَ الظُّلُماتِ إلى النُّورِ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 11] is: from the darkness of disbelief to the light of faith, because the proofs of disbelief are dark and unclear, while the proofs of Islam are plain and clear. His saying: ﴿قَدْ أحْسَنَ اللَّهُ لَهُ رِزْقًا﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 11] means: Allah has provided him with Paradise, whose bliss neither ceases nor passes away. Then He, Majestic and Mighty, mentioned what points to His oneness, and said: ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَماواتٍ ومِنَ الأرْضِ مِثْلَهُنَّ يَتَنَـزَّلُ الأمْرُ بَيْنَهُنَّ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 12]; so in every heaven and every earth there are creatures of His creation and an effective command of His command.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿لِتَعْلَمُوا أنَّ اللَّهَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾.

His saying: ﴿وَأنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أحاطَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا﴾ — ”عِلْمًا“ is accusative as an emphasizing maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of His saying ﴿وَأنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ أحاطَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عِلْمًا﴾ is: He has known everything with knowledge. Like it is: ﴿وَتَرى الجِبالَ تَحْسَبُها جامِدَةً وهي تَمُرُّ مَرَّ السَّحابِ﴾ [al-Naml: 88]; then He said: ﴿صُنْعَ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Naml: 88] as emphasis, because the meaning of His saying ﴿صُنْعَ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Naml: 88] is "Allah made the mountains pass as the clouds pass."
